```{r}
# import data (positive and negative mode data from GNPS2 export)
# this is only annotated dataset 
gnps2_neg_annotated <- read_tsv("./MSE1_HILIC_Neg_results.tsv")
gnps2_pos_annotated <- read_tsv("./MSE1_HILIC_Pos_results.tsv")

# import full quantification table from MZmine (both modes)
# this is full dataset 
mzmine_neg_full <- read_csv("./MSE1_Negative_spectra_quant.csv")
mzmine_pos_full <- read_csv("./MSE1_Positive_spectra_quant.csv")

# need to rename some columns from the mzmine files
# they are currently named after the original raw files, followed by Peak area 
# (example: 20260217-Ford-HILIC-XBridge-Amide-2_1x150mm-Negative-96.raw Peak area")
# I want to only keep the last term before the .raw (this is the sample ID)
mzmine_neg_full <- mzmine_neg_full %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ str_extract(.x, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=\\.raw)"),
    .cols = contains(".raw")
  ) # this works for the pattern "20260403_Ford_HILIC_Negative_QC02.raw Peak area"

mzmine_neg_renamed <- mzmine_neg_full %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ str_extract(.x, "[^-]+$"),
    .cols = contains("1x150mm")
  ) # this is to deal with the other pattern 

# verify this worked
names(mzmine_neg_renamed) 


# repeat with pos mode
mzmine_pos_full <- mzmine_pos_full %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ str_extract(.x, "(?<=_)[^_]+(?=\\.raw)"),
    .cols = contains(".raw")
  ) 

mzmine_pos_renamed <- mzmine_pos_full %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ str_extract(.x, "[^-]+$"),
    .cols = contains("1x150mm")
  ) 

# verify this worked
names(mzmine_pos_renamed) 


# need to remove the standards (not the same as QC)
mzmine_neg_renamed_nostandards <- mzmine_neg_renamed %>% dplyr::select(-Standard1, -Standard2, -Standard3, -Standard4)
mzmine_pos_renamed_nostandards <- mzmine_pos_renamed %>% dplyr::select(-Standard1, -Standard2, -Standard3, -ProcessBlank10, -`4`)

mzmine_neg_renamed_nostandards <- subset(mzmine_neg_renamed_nostandards, select = -`...200`) # ...200 is an empty column
mzmine_pos_renamed_nostandards <- subset(mzmine_pos_renamed_nostandards, select = -`...201`) # ...201 is an empty column

dim(mzmine_neg_renamed_nostandards) #14459 rows x 195 columns 
dim(mzmine_pos_renamed_nostandards) #10073 rows x 195 columns


# merge full neg with annotated neg
neg_with_annotations <- mzmine_neg_renamed_nostandards %>% 
  left_join(gnps2_neg_annotated %>% 
              dplyr::select(UniqueID, Compound_Name, superclass, class, subclass),
    by = c("row ID" = "UniqueID")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Annotation = ifelse(is.na(Compound_Name), "Unknown", Compound_Name),
    Annotated = ifelse(is.na(Compound_Name), "No", "Yes")
  )
# summary 
nrow(neg_with_annotations) # 14459 compounds 
sum(neg_with_annotations$Annotated == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE) # 199 annotated compounds (1.3% annotated from neg mode)

# merge full pos with annotated pos 
pos_with_annotations <- mzmine_pos_renamed_nostandards %>% 
  left_join(gnps2_pos_annotated %>% 
              dplyr::select(UniqueID, Compound_Name, superclass, class, subclass),
    by = c("row ID" = "UniqueID")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Annotation = ifelse(is.na(Compound_Name), "Unknown", Compound_Name),
    Annotated = ifelse(is.na(Compound_Name), "No", "Yes")
  )
# summary 
nrow(pos_with_annotations) # 10073 compounds 
sum(pos_with_annotations$Annotated == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE) # 174 annotated compounds (1.7% annotated from pos mode)

# make sure pos and neg have same number of columns before merging
ncol(pos_with_annotations) # 201
ncol(neg_with_annotations) # 201

## Merge pos and neg modes 
# add mode identifier and combine 
neg_with_annotations$Mode <- "negative"
pos_with_annotations$Mode <- "positive"

full_merged <- bind_rows(neg_with_annotations, pos_with_annotations)
ncol(full_merged) # confirming that new columns aren't being added to the left, but that they are truly combining 
nrow(full_merged) # 24532 total compounds 
sum(full_merged$Annotated =="Yes", na.rm = TRUE) # 373 annotated compounds (1.5% of total compounds annotated)

# need to change sample IDs so they don't have 0s in front of them 
full_merged <- full_merged %>%
  rename(
    `1` = `01`,
    `2` = `02`,
    `3` = `03`, 
    `4` = `04`,  
    `5` = `05`, 
    `6` = `06`, 
    `8` = `08`
  )

write_tsv(full_merged, "./metabolomics_full_merged.tsv")
```

```{r}
# filter with QC samples 
qc_sample_ids <- c("QC1", "QC2", "QC3", "QC4", "QC05", "QC06", "QC07", "QC08", "QC09", "QC10", 
             "QC11", "QC12", "QC13") 

# Pivot to create a 'sample_id' column
# Assuming your data has metadata columns and then sample columns
long_data <- full_merged %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^[0-9]|QC"), # Adjust this regex to match ONLY your sample columns
    names_to = "sample_id", 
    values_to = "intensity"
  )

nrow(long_data) # 4464824 total compounds across all samples 
# (note that this counts each appearance of every compound as a new row; so if compound A is in 3 samples, it counts as 3 rows)

# Compounds in >60% of QC samples AND low CV (<30% variation across QC samples; ensures reproducibility)
qc_filtered_data <- long_data %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% qc_sample_ids) %>%
  group_by(`row m/z`, `row retention time`, Annotation, superclass, class, subclass) %>%
  summarise(
    qc_prevalence = mean(!is.na(intensity)),
    qc_cv = sd(intensity, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(intensity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(qc_prevalence > 0.6 & qc_cv < 0.3) %>% # 60% detection, <30% CV
  # inner_join back to the long_data to filter your actual samples
  inner_join(long_data, by = c("row m/z", "row retention time", "Annotation", "superclass", "class", "subclass")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(intensity)) # might come back and play around with this (40$ CV?) 

nrow(qc_filtered_data) # 51870 compounds (keeping only 1% of total compounds)

# Annotated compounds only (no "Unknown")
annotated_data <- qc_filtered_data %>%
  filter(!grepl("Unknown", Annotation, ignore.case = TRUE))
nrow(annotated_data) # 6370 annotated compounds 

# need to remove QC after filtering to remove rows that have NAs 
annotated_data_clean <- annotated_data %>% 
  filter(!sample_id %in% qc_sample_ids)

nrow(annotated_data_clean) # 5915 total compounds (again, this counts each appearance of a compound as a row)
```

```{r}
# need to create a new column where I combine row m/z and row retention time for the "taxa" table I will eventually create
mzRT_annotated_data_clean <- annotated_data_clean %>% 
  dplyr::select(`row m/z`, `row retention time`, sample_id, intensity) %>% 
  unite(
    col = "mz_rt", # name of new column
    `row m/z`, `row retention time`, # columns to merge
    sep = "_", # separator
    remove = TRUE # remove old columns
  )

# I need to un-pivot the data (move from the long to wide format so that each sample ID is a row and each mz_rt is a column)
mzRT_annotated_data_clean <- mzRT_annotated_data_clean %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = mz_rt,    # Values in this column become column headers
    values_from = intensity # Values in this column fill the cells
  )
dim(mzRT_annotated_data_clean) # 169 x 36 (so 35 unique annotated compounds across 169 samples)

# final data wrangling steps so phyloseq will accept this :) 

# set sample IDs as row names and remove the sample_id column 
otu_mat <- mzRT_annotated_data_clean %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")
# convert to a numeric matrix 
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_mat)
# create the phyloseq OTU table object 
OTU = otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = FALSE)


# now creating the "taxa" table for the phyloseq object, where the m/z_RT is matched to the annotation information 
# first need to create tibble with mz_rt and annotations 
mzRT_annotated_data_clean_2 <- annotated_data_clean %>% 
  dplyr::select(`row m/z`, `row retention time`, Annotation, superclass, class, subclass) %>% 
  unite(
    col = "mz_rt", # name of new column
    `row m/z`, `row retention time`, # columns to merge
    sep = "_", # separator
    remove = TRUE # remove old columns
  )

# un-pivot again so no duplicate mz_RT values 
tax_wide <- mzRT_annotated_data_clean_2 %>%
  dplyr::select(mz_rt, Annotation, superclass, class, subclass) %>%
  distinct(mz_rt, .keep_all = TRUE) # Ensures one row per feature
  
dim(tax_wide) # 35 x 5 (so 35 unique annotated compounds across the 4 "taxonomic" levels)

# convert mz_RT to rownames and make a matrix
tax_mat <- tax_wide %>%
  column_to_rownames("mz_rt") %>% 
  as.matrix()

TAX <- tax_table(tax_mat)

# now I just need metadata
# recall you already imported metadata:
mse1

# confirm that you have the same # of samples here as you do in the otu table 
dim(mse1) # 169
dim(OTU) # 169 

# make sure rowname = sample ID (but keep sample ID in the metadata)
metadata_ready <- mse1 %>%
  mutate(sample_id_copy = ID) %>% # Make a copy
  column_to_rownames("sample_id_copy")   # Use the copy as row names

SAMPLES <- sample_data(metadata_ready)


# merge everything for full phyloseq object 
physeq_annotated <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX, SAMPLES)  

# check 
otu_df <- as.data.frame(otu_table(physeq_annotated))
otu_df # looks good 

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(physeq_annotated))
tax_df # looks good 

sample_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_annotated))
sample_df # looks good; sample IDs are in the order that the OTU table is in 

# save 
save(physeq_annotated, file="./exudates_phyloseq_annotated.Rdata")
```

jsd full distance matrix 
```{r}
dist_jsd <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_full, "jsd") 
dist_jsd_matrix <- as.matrix(dist_jsd)

Stress <- sample_data(physeq_full)$Stress_ID

# compute mean distance (and spread) from control to each treatment 
control_label <- "Control"  
treats          <- unique(Stress)
other_treats    <- treats[treats != control_label]

# Storage
res_jsd <- data.frame(
  Treatment = character(),
  Distance_to_Control_jsd = numeric(),
  SE = numeric(),
  n_pairs = integer(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (trt in other_treats) {
  # Indices of samples in Control
  s_ctrl  <- which(Stress == control_label)
  # Indices of samples in treatment `trt`
  s_trt   <- which(Stress == trt)
  
  # All Control–Treatment distances (each Control rep vs each trt rep)
  d_ctl_trt_jsd <- dist_jsd_matrix[s_ctrl, s_trt]
  
  # Mean and SE
  m <- mean(d_ctl_trt_jsd)
  se <- sd(d_ctl_trt_jsd) / sqrt(length(d_ctl_trt_jsd))
  n_pairs <- length(d_ctl_trt_jsd)
  
  res_jsd <- rbind(res_jsd, data.frame(
    Treatment = trt,
    Distance_to_Control_jsd = m,
    SE = se,
    n_pairs = n_pairs, 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# now add a column for the distance between each rep and the control 
res_jsd$dist_to_mean_reps_jsd <- vector("list", nrow(res_jsd))

for (i in 1:nrow(res_jsd)) {
  trt <- res_jsd$Treatment[i]
  s_ctrl <- which(Stress == control_label)
  s_trt <- which(Stress == trt)
  
  mean_dist_per_trt_rep <- apply(dist_jsd_matrix[s_trt, s_ctrl, drop = FALSE], 1, mean) - res_jsd$Distance_to_Control_jsd[i]
  res_jsd$dist_to_mean_reps_jsd[[i]] <- mean_dist_per_trt_rep
}


# sort x axis 
treatment_order <- factor(c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                          "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP", 
                          "Drought_Herbicide", "Antibiotic_Drought", "Antibiotic_Herbicide",
                          "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                          "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                          "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"), 
                         levels = c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                                   "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP", 
                                   "Drought_Herbicide", "Antibiotic_Drought", "Antibiotic_Herbicide",
                                   "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"))

res_jsd$Treatment <- factor(res_jsd$Treatment, levels = levels(treatment_order))

# plot with variation around the mean 
jsd_mean_distances_se <- ggplot(res_jsd, aes(x = Treatment, y = Distance_to_Control_jsd)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Distance_to_Control_jsd - SE,
        ymax = Distance_to_Control_jsd + SE),
    width = 0.2,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  ylab("Mean JSD distance to Control") +
  xlab("Treatment") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# save data to plot together with microbiome data
metabolomic_jsd_data <- jsd_mean_distances_se$data
saveRDS(metabolomic_jsd_data, file = "./metabolomic_jsd_data.rds")
```

)
